players.product: optical fiber, fiber cable, and connectivity solutions for AI data center scale-out and scale-up networks; solar polysilicon, wafers, and modules

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ed Schlesinger, Q2 segments: Glass Innovations sales $1.46 billion, up $20 million or 1% (higher display glass sales), net income $354 million, up 9%; Automotive sales $471 million, up 2% versus a global vehicle market down 2%, net income $82 million, up 4%, with diesel up 3% year over year and 13% sequentially on improving North American Class 8 orders; Solar sales $438 million, up $207 million or 90%, with a net loss of $7 million including an additional $30 million of expense versus Q1 as the solar wafer factory underwent an extended maintenance shutdown, transitioning to a permanent power system while repairing and upgrading production equipment; Life Sciences and Emerging Growth Businesses sales up 8% and net income up 13% sequentially. Carrier sales grew 1% — CEO Wendell Weeks: 'It's just customer timing'; first-half 2026 carrier sales were up about 17% versus first-half 2025 and 'That's going to continue to be a nice growth rate' (CFO: carrier expected to grow sales mid-single digits longer term, driven by fiber-to-the-home and data center interconnect); on new incremental opportunities 'they're coming to us almost always first.'
quarterly_data.figure: Glass Innovations $1.46B (+1%); Automotive $471M (+2%); Solar $438M (+90%, net loss $7M); carrier +1% (H1 +17%)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Wendell Weeks: 'From the beginning of Springboard, we have more than tripled enterprise sales'; Q2 enterprise sales grew 65% to $1.27 billion and 'our Gen AI product sales nearly doubled' (CFO Ed Schlesinger: 'The portion of enterprise sales related to AI data centers nearly doubled in the quarter'). On scale-up, today 100% copper: 'Optical is beginning to penetrate the scale-up network. This adds an entirely new optical network' — 'the timing of adoption and penetration are very difficult to predict.'
quarterly_data.figure: Enterprise $1.27B (+65%); Gen AI product sales nearly doubled; enterprise sales more than tripled since the start of Springboard

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Wendell Weeks on how the Springboard plan is built: business plans aim for a 70% confidence interval (a 70% chance of sales greater than or equal to the number); 2027-2030 assumptions include a forward rate of JPY 150 per US dollar, flat TV, IT and smartphone end markets with the impact of higher memory prices, declining ICE demand offset by more Corning auto content, a larger solar opportunity, new Gorilla Glass innovations and form factors, and accelerating fiber-to-the-home and data center interconnect growth in carrier; consumer electronics, solar, carrier, auto and life sciences are planned at a mid-single-digit CAGR in aggregate. The first phase of Springboard (to Q4 2026) is expected to deliver a 15% sales CAGR, accelerating to 19% (a 400 basis point increase) from 2027. CFO Ed Schlesinger: versus the Q4 2023 starting point, sales are up 45%, operating margin up 460 basis points, EPS up 100% and ROIC up 610 basis points; the high-confidence plan doubles the run rate from Q4 2025 through Q4 2030; operating margin to run 'at or above 20%' with an update later this year; ROIC (approximately 15%) to improve into the high teens; free cash flow expected to grow significantly as long-term agreements share the risk and cost of expansions with customers.
quarterly_data.figure: Plan assumes JPY 150 per USD; 15% CAGR to Q4 2026, then 19%; ROIC to high teens; operating margin at or above 20%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ed Schlesinger on the second half: the Q3 guide 'is not intended to imply any deceleration in growth' — similar year-over-year growth as Q2, with enterprise a significant component; below-normal seasonality is expected in memory-affected handhelds ('significantly weaker than the first half of the year', Corning to outperform on content per device) and a 'relatively muted' automotive market; solar profit improvement from Q2 to Q3 drives the implied margin step-up; the capex investment run rate increases into Q3 and Q4. In advanced optics he expects 'strong demand for advanced memory to support long-term demand from chip makers and semiconductor equipment suppliers for our solutions'; in display the memory-price impact is expected to be less significant. Solar: Corning continues to secure long-term customer commitments for polysilicon, wafers and modules, is 'the only U.S.-based polysilicon and wafer manufacturer', and targets a $3 billion revenue stream 'with profitability above the corporate average.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 similar YoY growth to Q2; solar toward a $3B revenue stream

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Wendell Weeks on photonics guidance: 'I don't think we guided anything for next year on photonics, just to be clear, right? We gave the longer term, $10 billion ... but we've yet to provide a specific number for you in photonics'; the company will update each quarter. On FAUs: fiber delivered to the faceplate sits in the enterprise MAP, while what is inside the faceplate, including the fiber array unit (FAU) harness, is in the photonics MAP — 'There is a lot more content than just those within that photonics map.'
quarterly_data.figure: no photonics number given for next year; photonics MAP $10B by 2030
